Reportable Communicable Diseases
 Monthly Report - December 2024

column1:
Source: Ontario Ministry of Health, integrated Public Health Information System (iPHIS), extracted [02/12/2025].
             Ontario Ministry of Health, Case and Contact Management System (CCM), extracted [06/27/2024].
1 Rate per 100,000 population. Population source:Statistics Canada, Centre for Demography, customized data (2019).
2 3-year average based on 2021-2023 data, rounded to the nearest integer.
3 Data entry of CPE is delayed due to operational concerns, and is lagging up to six months.
4 This category captures cases with positive HBV markers with insufficient evidence to be classified; these are most likely carriers.
5 Excludes syphilis, infectious and syphilis, early congenital.
6 Due to changes in provincial guidance as of June 2024, health units are not required to entered sporadic cases of COVID-19, so this is an underestimate of the true burden of COVID-19.
7 Mpox was designated a Disease of Public Health Significance (DOPHS) on June 16, 2022.
8 TB cases included in this report are classified by diagnosis date.
9 Anaplasmosis, Babesiosis, and Powassan virus were designated as Diseases of Public Health Significance (DOPHS) on July 1, 2023.
10 Due to operational constraints related to the COVID-19 Response, Encephalitis/Meningitis reports (from January 2021 onwards) were not entered into the provincial reporting system (iPHIS).
11 Number of outbreaks and not number of cases counted.
